question: Why does a sensitive electronic instrument protected by a metallic case (electrostatic shielding) remain unaffected by strong external electric fields?

options.A: Because the metal reflects the electric field lines.
options.B: Because the electric field lines pass through the metal without affecting the interior.
options.C: Because induced charges on the metal surface create a field that exactly cancels the external field inside the conductor.
options.D: Because the metal case is a perfect insulator.
